supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for leo.martins from 203.0.113.250, both with an incorrect-password status, at 13:40:30 and 13:42:01 UTC.
At 13:43:21 UTC, the domain controller recorded a successful network logon for leo.martins from the same IP address, shortly after the failures.

The failure-then-success sequence from a source not identified among the inventoried hosts is consistent with an unauthorized attempt that obtained valid credentials. The provided environment context says there is no VPN and remote administration is only performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records establish network logon events on the domain controller, but do not identify the person or device behind the source address.
The source address is 203.0.113.250, a documentation-range address; these records do not establish the real source address or its location.
The available records do not show what resources, if any, were accessed after the successful logon.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish whether the successful logon was authorized or whether leo.martins's credentials were compromised.
The evidence does not establish the real-world origin of the source address.
The evidence does not establish what activity followed the successful network logon.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate the source address and logon time with firewall, network, DHCP, and endpoint telemetry to identify the originating device.
Review domain-controller and resource-access logs after 13:43 UTC for actions associated with the successful logon.
Confirm with leo.martins whether the logon was expected and check for other authentication activity involving the account.
